scopeRule: Natural gas pipelines tied to the US data center buildout, at ANY length (Baird 2026-10-16, no floor): a transmission line, lateral, loop or expansion whose sourced purpose is to supply a data center, a data center campus, or a gas power plant built for one. Compression-only expansions tied to data centers count (LengthKnown 0). OUT: pipe inside the plant fence, local utility distribution mains, field gathering, and power-plant laterals with no data center tie (those are monitor when under 25 km; 25 km or more was covered by the 2026-10-02 discovery). Crude, NGL and refined-product lines are out of scope. If you cannot establish a length, still emit it and say 'length unknown'.
vetRule: (d) DATA CENTER RULES (Baird 2026-10-16, docs/plans/2026-10-16_us-gas-datacenter-subfloor.md). 1 (loosened later on 2026-10-16): DataCenter = yes with a validated ref that names THIS pipeline and mentions data centers at all as a demand driver or a reason for the project (the filing, the developer, the shipper, EIA, or press). One of several named drivers counts; so does a shipper whose demand for this project the source ties to data centers. Data center talk that is company-wide and not about this project, comes only from opponents, or concerns another row leaves DataCenter blank with a note in researcher_notes. 2: a compression-only expansion tied to data centers is a new_row with LengthKnown = 0, LengthKnownUnits = mi (or km as the source states), Diameter blank, RouteType 'Capacity expansion only', RouteAccuracy 'no route', in the parent-system / SegmentName shape of (e); the parent row is not tagged for it. 3: no length floor for a pipeline tied to data centers; in-fence plant piping and utility distribution mains are out. A sourced line with no data center tie and under 25 km -> class monitor, monitor_reason 'no data center tie'. (e) EXPANSION ROWS: GEM tracks US expansion projects as their own rows, with PipelineName = the parent system's GEM PipelineName exactly as the roster spells it and SegmentName = the project (e.g. P2544 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline' / 'Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 2'). An expansion with no row of its own is a new_row in that shape, not a match to the parent system's row. A project that IS an existing row under another name is matched_existing. (f) EIA (sources/eia_pipeline_projects/NOTES.md): cite the DATED release that states the value as https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/<file> (newest is EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx; never the undated twin), sheet + Excel row in the note, url_verifier with --name set to the EIA project name. Local copies are in sources/eia_pipeline_projects/raw/. Pair EIA with a FERC order/filing, a state regulator document or an operator release when cheap. EIA 'Cost (millions)' -> stage the full number (450 -> 450000000, USD). EIA miles -> LengthKnown in mi, never converted. EIA 'Additional Capacity' is INCREMENTAL MMcf/d for an expansion. Status: Announced/Pre-filing/Applied/Approved -> proposed, Construction -> construction, Completed -> operating, On Hold -> shelved, Cancelled/Denied -> cancelled. Month cells are integers 1-12. (g) Country = United States; Puerto Rico is out of scope. Intrastate lines never appear in FERC: FERC silence is not an existence concern; check the state regulator (Texas RRC T-4 etc.). (h) Owner names in the ownership team's style: run scripts/entity_lookup.py and scripts/entity_style.py, adopt the team's spelling on an exact/alias hit only. Notes are plain language for a person: short sentences, sources named by what they are, no repo jargon, no em-dashes or arrows.

seedIntro:
Seeds come from three sources, named by the seed_id prefix and the 'SOURCE' label in each hint.
eia: a project from EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (2024 or later release, or in service 2024+) whose demand served or notes name data centers or power, with NO strong GEM match on the fresh crosswalk. 'weak crosswalk hints' list PIDs that may be the parent system or the same project under another name: check those first. An expansion of a GEM system with no row of its own is a candidate in the parent-system / SegmentName shape. A 'strong crosswalk match' seed (Nueva Era Dos, PLUSS) is in the list because it is short power-demand pipe Baird named: decide whether the match is right or the project deserves its own row. Power demand alone, no data center tie, under 25 km -> monitor 'no data center tie'.
lead: a named lead from a web survey of data center pipelines. The hint carries what the survey found and its sources; verify everything yourself.
plant: a GOGPT gas power plant built for a data center (GEM's own plant tracker, so it is a LEAD, never a ref). Your job is to find HOW THE PLANT GETS ITS GAS. The hint lists the nearest GGIT routes with distances. Each plant seed ends in one of four outcomes; start the ledger reason with the outcome code:
  NEW_LATERAL: a dedicated new lateral or pipeline (any length) that GEM lacks -> candidate + 'queued'.
  EXISTING_ROW: it is supplied directly by an existing roster row (a tap on that line, or a lateral that already has a row) -> 'matched' with matched_project_id and the evidence URL naming both the pipeline and the plant. This is a DataCenter tag lead for that row, NOT an alias: never suggest the plant name as an OtherEnglishNames.
  ONSITE_NO_PIPE: supplied by an on-site, in-fence or behind-the-meter tap with no new pipe, or by a utility distribution main -> 'monitor' with what you found.
  NOT_FOUND: no source says how it gets gas -> 'monitor' saying what you searched. A 'gogpt-notes' plant that is not actually built for a data center (the notes only mention utility load or say it is not for a data center) -> 'dropped' with why.
Several seeds may be one project (an EIA lateral, a lead and the plant it feeds): give them the same candidate and say so.
monitor: a candidate the 10-16 slice run vetted to monitor (an existing lead with its own slug). The hint carries the values and the reason it was held. Re-research it from scratch: find endpoints, length and a concrete step, and test the data center tie against the loosened ruling 1 (data centers mentioned at all as a reason for the project count). If it now qualifies, it is a candidate + 'queued'; otherwise 'monitor' with what was searched.
dropped: a seed the slice run dropped. Check the drop reason again; reverse it only on a source.
seedSearch: COMPREHENSIVE SEARCH (required for every seed; a seed that ends monitor must list in its reason each source below that was checked and what it showed, in plain words): (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, newest release (sources/eia_pipeline_projects/raw/, data/eia_projects_latest.csv), by operator, county and plant name; (2) FERC: eLibrary and Federal Register searches for the plant, campus, developer and county, including CP dockets and blanket certificate prior notices (short laterals and taps are usually prior notices); (3) the state regulator: the public utility commission or siting board docket (Ohio Power Siting Board, Virginia SCC, Kentucky PSC, Georgia PSC, Indiana IURC, Wisconsin PSC, Louisiana PSC and the like), and for Texas the Railroad Commission T-4 permits and its pipeline GIS viewer for the county; (4) the state air permit or its public notice (TCEQ, Ohio EPA, Pennsylvania DEP and the like), which often names the gas supplier and the lateral; (5) the utility's integrated resource plan or rate case if a utility builds the plant; (6) county and city records and local news: zoning and planning agendas, commission minutes, road-crossing or easement notices; (7) the developer's, the hyperscaler's and the midstream company's releases, project pages, investor decks and earnings-call transcripts (Energy Transfer, Kinder Morgan, Williams, Enbridge, TC Energy, Boardwalk, DT Midstream, EQT, Atmos, ONEOK, Targa, Tallgrass, Southwest Gas, local distribution companies); (8) trade press (Pipeline and Gas Journal, Natural Gas Intelligence, RBN, Data Center Dynamics, Utility Dive, E&E News). Search each in English with several name variants (plant, campus, code name, developer, county, nearest town). Do at least eight distinct searches per seed before NOT_FOUND. A blocked page is not a dead end: run python scripts/fetch.py <url> --head 4000, then the Wayback copy, before giving up on it. GOGPT and gem.wiki stay leads only, never refs. For eia: seeds, start from EIA's own row and cite the dated release URL https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/<file>.
